fields.title: Positioning: how you stand out in the customer's mind
fields.keyTakeaway: Positioning is choosing where you are intentionally worse. As long as a product is "better across all parameters", it lacks positioning, and in conversations, it gets compared on price.
fields.checkQuestion: "We are more convenient and cheaper than competitors." Why is this not positioning?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key node question: **what is our edge over competitors?**
fields.blocks/1/subtitle: A value curve instead of a feature list
fields.blocks/1/items/0: **X-axis** — factors the market compares: price, implementation speed, support, feature set, reliability.
fields.blocks/1/items/1: **Y-axis** — how heavily each player invests in each factor.
fields.blocks/1/items/2: **Your curve** should differ in shape, not height. A curve that is slightly higher everywhere means "the same thing, but more expensive".
fields.blocks/1/items/3: **Four actions:** what to eliminate entirely, what to reduce, what to raise, what to create anew.
fields.blocks/2/text: **Perceptual Map** solves a related task: shows how products are located in customer perception along two key dimensions. Importantly, the axes come from user words, not from your view of the market.
fields.blocks/3/text:
Factors: price, feature set, speed to first document, support, accounting integrations.

Major player: high on everything except onboarding speed — implementation takes two weeks.
Cheap player: low price, weak on everything else.

Reestr eliminates some features (no inventory tracking, no HR documents), reduces integrations to the single most popular one, and focuses heavily on one thing: first document in four minutes with zero implementation.

Website headline: "Invoices in four minutes, no implementation or training". It turns away large accounts — and that is a deliberate choice.
fields.blocks/4/text: "Better architecture", "in-house dev team" — these are not positioning: customers don't compare them. Simple test — would this come up when they explain the product to a colleague?
fields.blocks/4/title: The difference must be visible to the customer, not to you
fields.blocks/5/text: Positioning won't beat a product that solves the problem better. It decides who you are compared with and on what basis — and that is where its power ends.
